correctness.rationale: This PASS is for the corrected files, not the frozen formula. In the frozen example n=4, a=0.4,b=0, the first coefficient of u is 0.05, and r=0,s=1 in its own equality equation requires v's coefficient to be 0.05 exp(−iπ/4); the printed weights give 0.05 exp(+iπ/4), so they are feasible but not maximizing. The repair preserves the specified mask and uses j+1/2. It proves trace duality equality by the existence of a unitary mapping X to Y, equivalently equality of their Gram matrices, including singular weights. On the support, Fourier labels can be chosen in one centered contiguous interval of length L=n (odd) or L=n−1 (even), where h_r=exp(−iπr/n). For k=1,...,n−1, actual differences k and k−n occur in max(0,L−k) and max(0,L−(n−k)) pairs, and their ratios differ by a minus sign. Therefore only k=±1 survives in even dimension, while none of the nonconstant modes survive in odd dimension. At k=1 evaluating the harmonic at j+1/2 is precisely the required negative phase; at k=−1 use conjugacy. Nonnegativity cuts out all equally spaced side half-planes at distance one, without losing degenerate probabilities. Summing the same singular values verifies both scalar formulas, and a unit-vector/nuclear norm duality identifies the Schur norm. No other conclusion from the frozen statement is needed for the repair.

value.rationale: The corrected classification determines whether symmetry can break among norming probability weights for a basic Schur idempotent and exactly which boundary-supported normers occur. A regular polygon versus a unique maximizer is an explicit structural datum not present in the classical scalar maximum. The claim neither classifies all norming matrices nor rests on a sign correction alone.
